content: The National Institute of Statistics and Censuses of Argentina, known in Spanish as Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC), is a governmental agency in Argentina tasked with the collection and processing of statistical data. This institution is responsible for analyzing various economic and social indicators, including the inflation rate, consumer price index, and unemployment rate, among others. The INDEC operates under the supervision of multiple federal agencies and is directly overseen by the Secretaría de Programación Económica y Regional (Secretariat of Economic and Regional Planning), which is part of the Ministerio de Economía y Producción (Ministry of Economy and Production, MECON). Additionally, the INDEC coordinates the Sistema Estadístico Nacional (National Statistics System, SEN), which functions under principles of centralized regulation and governmental division. Within the SEN, national, provincial, and local statistical services collaborate. Each province has its own statistics bureau, known as Dirección de Estadística, which is managed by the provincial government and is responsible for collecting and processing data. In Argentina, national censuses are officially conducted every 10 years. Historical censuses have been carried out in the years 1869, 1895, 1914, 1947, 1960, 1970, 1980, 1991 (delayed due to budgetary issues), and 2001. Between these decennial censuses, data is continuously updated through a sampled survey called the Encuesta Permanente de Hogares (Permanent Homes' Survey). Comprehensive official reports are published every six months. The origins of Argentina's national statistical system date back to 1894, with the establishment of the Dirección General de Estadística (General Directorate of Statistics) as a division of the Ministry of Public Finances. In 1944, the Consejo Nacional de Estadística y Censos (National Council of Statistics and Censuses) was created, operating under the Ministry of the Interior and the National Presidential Office. Subsequent agencies were formed in 1950, 1952, and 1956, culminating in the establishment of the Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC) in 1968 through Law 17622 and Decrees 3110/70 and 1831/93. In January 2007, controversy arose when the head of INDEC resigned, and a new director was appointed by the Ministry of Economy. This led to significant unrest among INDEC employees, who expressed dissatisfaction over what they perceived as a violation of the agency's autonomy. They accused the Minister of Economy, under Felisa Miceli, of manipulating inflation indicators to unlawfully report rates below one percent.
